identity.title: Estimating sizes of faint, distant galaxies in the submillimetre regime
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper we will build on the work by (cite: decarli2014), using the same data, but extending the analysis to focus on the sizes of the stacked sources.

targets.name: K20, sBzK, DRG, ERO samples in ECDFS (stacked) and 99 ALESS SMGs

evidence.quote: The MUSYC catalogue is a $K$-band flux limited sample, covering a $30\ensuremath{'}\times{}30\ensuremath{'}$ area of the ECDFS

distance_source.value: photometric redshifts, Taylor et al. 2009 / EAZY

evidence.quote: The MUSYC catalogue is a $K$-band flux limited sample, covering a $30\ensuremath{'}\times{}30\ensuremath{'}$ area of the ECDFS

question.value: What are the typical sizes and flux densities of z~2 star-forming galaxies (DRG, ERO, sBzK, K20) measured by uv-stacking ALESS ALMA 344 GHz data with uv-domain model fitting?

evidence.quote: We measure the sizes of redshift $\sim2$ star-forming galaxies by stacking data from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.1.00294.S.
The observations are tuned to a frequency of 344 GHz and have a typical resolution around 1$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$6 $\times$ 1$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$2.
With the $uv$-coverage of our observations (18-160 m)
The median value of the noise (standard deviation) in the centre of each pointing is $\sim0.4$mJy/beam.
observed during ALMA Cycle 0 between October and November 2011

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: ALESS survey data, same as Decarli et al. 2014; 88 good-quality pointings

evidence.quote: As such our data consist of 88 “good quality” pointings

other_facilities.name: MUSYC / Spitzer IRAC / Taiwan ECDFS NIR survey

provided.value: Photometric catalogue, photometric redshifts, stellar masses

evidence.quote: The selection is based on the photometric catalogue of the ECDFS assembled using the same procedure as (cite: simpson2014)

provided.value: z-band images for stellar sizes and morphology model

evidence.quote: The inner parts of the ECDFS are covered by the GOODS-S survey (cite: Giavalisco2004), with Hubble Space Telescope (*HST*) observations in $z$-band

provided.value: Stacked SPIRE flux densities from Decarli et al. 2014 used for dust SED

evidence.quote: (cite: decarli2014) stacked each of the four samples in the three *Herschel* SPIRE bands.

what.value: Stacked Herschel SPIRE flux densities for the four samples

evidence.quote: (cite: decarli2014) stacked each of the four samples in the three *Herschel* SPIRE bands.

what.value: ALESS SMG sub-mm positions (main catalogue, 99 sources)

evidence.quote: We use the sub-mm positions from the main catalogue from (cite: hodge2013) (99 sources).

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Simulated clumpy-morphology and HST z-band-based ALMA datasets (visibilities zeroed, model plus CASA sm noise added), incl. a Cycle 3 C36-5 configuration

evidence.quote: We take the raw ALESS data set and set all visibilities to zero, then we add the model and noise to the data set.

task.value: CASA 4.4 imaging and cleaning of each pointing, only for bright source model

evidence.quote: The data is imaged and cleaned using Common Astronomy Software Applications package[^2] (CASA) version 4.4.
Each pointing is imaged separately with a cell size of 0$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$2 and cleaned down to a depth 1.8 mJy/beam.

primary_beam_correction.value: CASA 4.4 Airy model, FWHM ~17.5 arcsec; stacking weights = A_N^2

evidence.quote: an Airy pattern with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 1.17$\frac{\lambda}{D} \approx 17\mbox{\ensuremath{.\!\!^{\prime\prime}}}{}5$

what.value: Data selection (88 good-quality pointings, exclusion criteria)

evidence.quote: All pointings with central noise $>0.6$ mJy/beam or beam axis ratio $>2$ are excluded from the analysis, see (cite: hodge2013) for more details.

what.value: Sample selection same as Decarli et al.

evidence.quote: In this paper we extend the analysis of (cite: decarli2014), using the same sample selection.
The samples are stacked using the $uv$-stacking algorithm described in (cite: lindroos2015).

unstated_but_needed: Calibration details of ALESS data (pipeline/manual, CASA version of calibration, flux scale)
Exact catalogue source positions and sample membership lists
Source code of the uv-stacking implementation
Details of visibility weight recalculation bin sizes
Herschel SPIRE flux values for SED fits

analysis_steps.goal: Select samples and estimate stellar mass

method.value: Colour/photo-z selection (K20, sBzK, DRG, ERO) with K_Vega<20, z>1; PEGASE 2 SED fitting with four templates, lowest chi2

evidence.quote: We limit all samples with $\ensuremath{K_\mathrm{Vega}}< 20$, $z>1$, and further limit the samples as follows:
all assuming Kroupa IMF, we fit for stellar mass

method.value: Clean model from each pointing, excluding sources within 1 arcsec of stacking positions, subtracted from uv data; weights recalculated from scatter

evidence.quote: A model for the bright sources is built from the clean model, excluding all sources within 1$''$ of a stacking position.
cleaned down to a depth 1.8 mJy/beam

validation.value: Bias test with inserted point sources

evidence.quote: By inserting and stacking point sources in the ALESS data, using the method described in section [4.4](#sec:uncertainties), we evaluate biases in the stacking result.

method.value: Weighted average of visibilities phase-shifted to source positions, weights = primary beam attenuation squared; astrometry shifted by 0.3 arcsec in dec

evidence.quote: all stacked datasets were phase rotated with 0$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$3 in declination.

key_parameters.value: flag baselines <18.2 m (sBzK, DRG) and <21 m (K20, ERO)

evidence.quote: we flag all baseline shorter than $18.2\,\mathrm{m}$ for the sBzK and DRG samples

validation.value: Stacked all SMGs: Gaussian fit gives 4.2±0.14 mJy and 0.4±0.06 arcsec, consistent with Simpson et al. 2015

evidence.quote: This agrees well with (cite: simpson2015), which found typical sizes (FWHM) of SMGs between 0$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$3 and 0$.\!\!^{\prime\prime}$4.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit point-source and Gaussian models in uv-domain

method.value: Least-squares fit of point source and circular Gaussian to all non-flagged visibilities with weights, flux positive

evidence.quote: The models are fitted in the $uv$-domain to our stacked sources using the least square minimizer package Ceres .
The fit is terminated at the first to occur within 50 iterations

fitting.value: Levenberg-Marquardt chi2 minimization, 2 free parameters (flux, FWHM)

evidence.loc: Flux densities and sizes of the stacked sources
evidence.quote: In the plot is shown the fit from the Gaussian model, with two free parameters: the total flux density and the FWHM size.

validation.value: Compared to Vidal et al. size-limit formula; beta 0.4-0.5

evidence.quote: Using this formula we find our size error to be consistent with a $\beta$ between 0.4 and 0.5.

method.value: Monte Carlo insertion of random sources (100 runs) and bootstrap resampling of galaxies (1000 runs; errors from CDF at 0.159/0.841)

evidence.quote: This procedure is repeated a 100 times for each sample and model

method.value: Offsets from 11 galaxies with peak SNR>5; offset modelled as circular Gaussian FWHM 0.36 arcsec, deconvolved from sizes

evidence.quote: the offset between the submm and measured optical position can be modelled as a circular Gaussian with a FWHM of $0.36^{+0.06}_{-0.09}$

analysis_steps.goal: Fit dust SED and derive SFR

method.value: Modified blackbody with beta fixed 1.6, free T and L_IR, chi2 fit using stacked ALMA and Herschel SPIRE; SFR=1.3e-10 L_IR

evidence.quote: The value of $\beta$ is fixed to 1.6.
The total IR luminosity ($L_\mathrm{IR}$) is calculated between 8 $\mu$m and 1000 $\mu$m
The dust emission is fitted using a $\chi^2$ minimization, with two free parameters, $T$ and $L_\mathrm{IR}$. The value of $\beta$ is fixed to 1.6. Each data point is weighted by $\sigma^{-2}$.

validation.value: Compared to Tacconi et al. 2013 main sequence

evidence.quote: The measured values fall close to the best-fit “main sequence” for star-forming galaxies at similar redshifts, (e.g. the (cite: tacconi2013) parametrization for comparison).

method.value: Simulated clumpy model (3 clumps, 0.7 mJy each) and HST z-band-based model on ALESS and Cycle 3 C36-5 uv-coverage; stack identically

evidence.quote: For each source in the sample we generate 3 clumps, i.e., 3 point sources.

validation.value: Recovered flux 2.3±0.2 mJy vs input 2.1 mJy

evidence.quote: The Gaussian model recovers an average flux density for the stacked sources of $2.3\pm0.2$ mJy, compared to the input flux density for the simulation of 2.1 mJy per source.

used_for.value: imaging, clean models, primary beam model, simulator (sm)

evidence.quote: Common Astronomy Software Applications package[^2] (CASA) version 4.4
using the least square minimizer package Ceres .
The stellar-mass estimates are done using PEGASE 2
estimated using EAZY (cite: brammer2008)
with stacked sizes between $0\mbox{\ensuremath{.\!\!^{\prime\prime}}}65$ and $0\mbox{\ensuremath{.\!\!^{\prime\prime}}}73$
we find deconvolved sizes for our samples between $0\mbox{\ensuremath{.\!\!^{\prime\prime}}}54$ and $0\mbox{\ensuremath{.\!\!^{\prime\prime}}}64$
with a flux density $4.2\pm0.14$ mJy

results_numeric.quantity: Simulated clumpy flux with ALESS baselines

evidence.quote: The Gaussian model recovers an average flux density for the stacked sources of $2.3\pm0.2$ mJy

findings_qualitative.value: Stacked sources are extended; sub-mm sizes agree with HST z-band sizes; short baselines are essential to recover total stacked flux density.

evidence.quote: This highlights the importance of short baselines to recover the full flux density of high-redshift galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: z~2 star-forming galaxies are extended at 344 GHz
claims.experiment: uv-stacking and Gaussian uv-model fit for four samples
claims.finding: Typical sizes ~5-6 kpc, matching z-band sizes

evidence.quote: We find that the typical sizes of these galaxies are $\sim0\mbox{\ensuremath{.\!\!^{\prime\prime}}}6$

claims.experiment: Compare uv model fitting to point-source and image stacking
claims.result: Gaussian fluxes 20-40% higher than Decarli et al.
claims.finding: Model fitting recovers full flux if short baselines are available

evidence.quote: we find flux densities which are 20 to 40 per cent higher.
we measure an average flux density of only 90  $\umu$

why_this_method.value: uv-stacking avoids combining differently restored images, allowing deconvolution of source size

evidence.quote: Using $uv$-stacking, we combine the data in the $uv$-domain, and the beam can be directly calculated from the new $uv$-coverage.

limitations_admitted.value: GEMS z-band less deep, possibly underestimating stellar sizes; bright source subtraction incomplete on shortest baselines

evidence.quote: As such is possible that we are missing low flux surface density emission, and underestimating the size of these galaxies.

referee_caveats_inferred: Optical-submm offset modelled from only 11 galaxies
Bright source subtraction based on clean models leaves residuals, handled by flagging short baselines
Fixed beta and few SED points

data_public_as_stated.value: ALESS data 2011.1.00294.S cited; public status not explicitly stated

fixed.new: By inserting and stacking point sources in the ALESS data, using the method described in section [4.4](#sec:uncertainties), we evaluate biases in the stacking result.
In the plot is shown the fit from the Gaussian model, with two free parameters: the total flux density and the FWHM size.
The dust emission is fitted using a $\chi^2$ minimization, with two free parameters, $T$ and $L_\mathrm{IR}$. The value of $\beta$ is fixed to 1.6. Each data point is weighted by $\sigma^{-2}$.
The measured values fall close to the best-fit “main sequence” for star-forming galaxies at similar redshifts, (e.g. the (cite: tacconi2013) parametrization for comparison).
The Gaussian model recovers an average flux density for the stacked sources of $2.3\pm0.2$ mJy, compared to the input flux density for the simulation of 2.1 mJy per source.
